schedule.intro: Open an event for what to wear, directions and more.

travel.intro: Most guests fly into Toronto Pearson (YYZ). The wedding venues are all within an hour of the airport.

airports.name: Toronto Pearson International
airports.tips: Largest airport with the most direct flights, including to India.

airports.name: Billy Bishop Toronto City
airports.tips: Small downtown airport with short lines; mostly domestic and US flights.

airports.name: John C. Munro Hamilton International
airports.tips: Budget carriers; quietest option and closest to the Burlington venue.

gettingAround.title: Rideshare and taxis
gettingAround.text: Uber and Lyft operate throughout the area. Expect [$45 to $70] from YYZ to the hotels.

gettingAround.title: Car rental
gettingAround.text: Rental cars are available at all airports. A car is helpful if you plan to explore. Parking at every event is free or inexpensive.

gettingAround.title: Transit
gettingAround.text: UP Express and GO Transit connect the airport and downtown. Transit does not reach the venues, so plan on a car or our shuttles.

international.title: Travelling from outside Canada
international.text: Check entry requirements early. Visitors from visa-exempt countries need an eTA (about CAD $7, usually approved within minutes). Others may need a visitor visa, which can take weeks. We are happy to provide an invitation letter; message a coordinator.

aroundTown.name: Niagara Falls
aroundTown.text: About 75 minutes away. A classic day trip.

aroundTown.name: CN Tower and downtown Toronto
aroundTown.text: Skyline views, museums and great food.

aroundTown.name: Gerrard India Bazaar
aroundTown.text: Toronto's Little India: sweets, saris and supper.

aroundTown.name: Burlington Waterfront Trail
aroundTown.text: A calm lakeside walk five minutes from the venue.

faq.q: What are Mehendi, Haldi and Vidhi, and the wedding?
faq.a: Mehendi is henna at CISE. Haldi and Vidhi is the blessing at CISE. The wedding ceremony is at the Grand Imperial. Each invitation lists the events you are invited to.
The Baraat is the groom's joyful procession to the ceremony, with drums, dancing and family. It begins at 3:30 PM on the wedding day.
Yes, everyone is welcome. Wear shoes you can dance in, bring water, and follow the dhol. No experience required.

faq.q: What should I wear to each event?
faq.a: Mehendi: colourful and comfortable. Haldi and Vidhi: old yellow or white clothes you can stain. Wedding: traditional Indian or formal. See each event on the Schedule page for swatches.

faq.q: I have never worn Indian clothes. Where can I get some?
faq.a: Message a coordinator and we will point you to shops in the GTA, or to rentals. You are also welcome in formal Western attire.
The wedding menu is fully vegetarian, with vegan and Jain options. Please note any allergies on your RSVP.

faq.q: Do I need to cover my head at the ceremony?
faq.a: Head coverings are welcome but not required. If you would like one, we will have scarves and caps at the entrance. Please remove your shoes before entering the ceremony space.
About 90 minutes. We will have a program explaining each ritual, and seating for everyone.
Yes! Children are welcome at all events. There will be a quiet room near the ceremony.

faq.q: Do you have a registry? What about cash gifts?
faq.a: Your presence is the best gift. If you would like to give something, see the Registry page. Cash or cheques are traditional and appreciated.
Every venue has free or inexpensive parking on site. Accessible spaces are beside each main entrance.
Yes. A shuttle runs from the block hotels to the ceremony and back. See Travel for times; reserve seats on your RSVP.
Please arrive 15 to 20 minutes early so you can find your seat before each event begins.
